title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1LC1RC_1LA1RD_1LD0RB_0LC0LF_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1LC1RC_1LA1RD_1LD0RB_0LC0LF_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine's cycle is understood (a block of ones multiplied by about 3/2, with a remainder mod 6 written into a short tail); the two sub-rounds are proved in Lean for all counts, the cycle map is computed, and the run has been followed to 1013 steps without a halt. Which tails could lead to the halting pattern is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,751 cells have been visited and 34,326 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.071).

claims.title: The two sub-rounds, for all counts
claims.text: Absorption: B>0 0 0 1^X 0 (110)^k R becomes B>0 0 0 1^(X+9) 0 (110)^(k-2) R for X = 3x + 11 (any x, k ≥ 3, any tape R). Conversion: for X = 3x + 9 the block becomes 1^4 0 1 (101)^(x+3) 1 1.

claims.title: The cycle map
claims.text: From an S-state B>0 0 0 1^X 0 T the next S-state has X' = (3X + c)/2, with c and the new tail depending on X mod 6 and on T (table on the explainer); checked by direct simulation from constructed tapes, and along the run from blank tape to step 3.6·108.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>13</sup> steps
claims.text: The accelerated simulator of the shared tools (cycle rules proved by symbolic simulation) runs 10<sup>13</sup> steps without a halt; the S-state at step 2,710,634,500,213 has X = 2,125,526.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The machine halts exactly in state C on a 0 with three 1s to its left. None of the S-states tried (all X mod 6, all tails of at most three blocks of at most 9 ones) halts before the next S-state, so halting would need a tail not seen yet.

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state A reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 2 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (38 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 26 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 100,179 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 32,285 of the run (A = (empty), U = 110, m = 81, B = 13 0 16): 100,179 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 29,307 bits (about 1017,645 steps of the machine). 204 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 4,246 cells. The iteration stops there, at a context too large for the six simulations (a second long block has formed); this is a limit of the tool, not an event of the machine.

claims.title: No halting class among 530 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 530 contexts expanded, 530 found, to depth 184. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 36 contexts longer than 300 cells were not expanded.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known; the tail update has not been put in closed form.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LF_1LC1RD_1RA1LA_0RA0RE_0RC---_1RF0LC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine keeps one long block of ones and multiplies its length by about 3/2 per cycle, like a Collatz map, writing what is left over into a short tail. This page runs the real machine and explains the cycle.

facts.text: Absorption and conversion, proved for all counts.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state A reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 2 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 26 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 32,285 of the run (A = (empty), U = 110, m = 81, B = 13 0 16): 100,179 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 29,307 bits (about 1017,645 steps of the machine). 204 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 4,246 cells. The iteration stops there, at a context too large for the six simulations (a second long block has formed); this is a limit of the tool, not an event of the machine.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 530 contexts expanded, 530 found, to depth 184. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 36 contexts longer than 300 cells were not expanded.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.071).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,751 cells (32,203 left of the start, 22 right), with a density of 1s of 0.767.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Multiply by 3/2, carry into a tail
html: At an S-state the tape is 0 0 1^X 0 T, head in state B on the blank cell at the left, T a short tail of blocks of ones. A cycle has three parts:

1. Conversion. B, C, D sweep right turning each 111 into 110: the block becomes about X/3 pairs 110.
  2. Absorption. Each sub-round builds a new block on the left, 9 ones longer, and removes two pairs: 1^X 0 (110)^k → 1^(X+9) 0 (110)^(k−2). After about X/6 sub-rounds the new block has about 3X/2 ones.
  3. The end reads what is left over (X mod 6) and rewrites the tail.
So X' = (3X + c)/2. The table gives c and the new tail for the first tails (by simulation from constructed S-states):

From blank tape the S-states have X = 41, 81, 150, 242, 377, 585, 915, 1395, 2115, 3195, 4815, 7245, 10890, 16352, 24542, …; while the tail is empty and X ≡ 3 (mod 6) the cycle is just X → (3X + 45)/2.

sections.heading: The tail decides, and it is not understood yet
html: The machine halts exactly when it is in state C on a 0 with three 1s to its left. The main block alone never does this; the end of a cycle reads and writes the tail, which is itself built of the same pieces (a block of 3j ones that is later turned into pairs) and grows very slowly: it is a second, slower counter fed by the first. Which tails could lead to the halting pattern is the open part. None tried (all tails of at most three blocks of at most 9 ones, every X mod 6) halts within one cycle, and the run has gone 1013 steps.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: One block of ones X grows by about 3/2 per cycle (converted to X/3 pairs 110, absorbed two at a time for +9 each), X' = (3X + c)/2 with c set by X mod 6 and a slowly growing tail; halting condition not understood.
